Objective: State what can be decided now versus blocked for the field-diagnostic copilot rollout, and name who owns each unresolved piece of work — business case, resistance, data, model risk, architecture — before any rollout date is committed to.

Body: **Trust boundary (holds regardless of downstream decisions).** The copilot is advisory only. It surfaces a diagnosis; the technician acts; the FSM system remains the record of truth. No design lets the copilot write to equipment state or close a work order without technician confirmation, until human-in-loop design is proven otherwise.

**Business case and headcount — Value Realization Lead, first.** No one has run a real value case against pilot data, and it's unknown whether projected payback assumes headcount reduction. The Value Realization Lead re-runs the business case using actual pilot throughput and error data, and states explicitly, in writing, whether the case assumes any reduction in technician headcount. Two weeks. This goes to the Executive Sponsor before any rollout commitment, not after.

**Technician and manager resistance — Domain Owner (once named) + Field Ops Manager, first.** Resistance from the people doing the work is information, not noise to manage past. The Field Ops Manager convenes a session with resisting technicians and line managers this week to surface specifically what they lose (diagnostic judgment, autonomy on calls) and what would have to be true for the copilot to be trustworthy to them. This shapes the escalation design below, not the other way around.

**Data pipeline — decided now.** Given known quality issues in pilot logs and no validated golden dataset, we do not fine-tune on pilot logs. We use retrieval-augmented generation over vetted service manuals and a validated golden set, with every answer citing its source. Fine-tuning is revisited only after the Data Readiness Lead validates the golden set against a stated accuracy threshold.

**Bias and model-risk audit — Model Risk Lead, distinct workstream.** This is not a subset of AI Act classification. The Model Risk Lead runs an audit of pilot outputs by equipment class, site, and technician tenure to check for systematic misdiagnosis patterns, independent of regulatory status, starting with the existing pilot transcripts.

**Model and platform selection — blocked.** Not chosen until: safety accuracy threshold (Domain Owner/Compliance), AI Act risk classification (safety-critical guidance may be high-risk), field connectivity constraints (low-connectivity sites may require edge caching, unverified), and cost per diagnosis (unmeasured) are settled. A model-abstraction gateway sits between application logic and any provider regardless — cheap now, expensive to retrofit.

**Integration blueprint — blocked on the process map.** The disputed-diagnosis escalation flow (Process Excellence Lead) is a system requirement: an override must write a logged, escalatable ticket into the FSM, not vanish silently. The FSM API contract and failure behavior (technician proceeds manually, event queued) can't be finalized until three real disputed cases are walked through this map.

**One-way doors.** Audit-trail data model/storage: high exit cost, decide with Data Readiness Lead and Security first. FSM integration contract: expensive to change once technicians build habit. Reversible: model choice, prompts, ranking heuristics — kept behind the gateway.

**Cost model.** [ASSUMPTION: cannot be built without pilot query volume, tokens/diagnosis, and corpus size — none provided.] Requested from Value Realization Lead before modeling cost at scale.

Citations: https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/high-level-summary/ (EU AI Act high-risk classification criteria, relevant to safety-critical diagnostic guidance)

Risks: No named business owner exists; an integration blueprint finalized against a phantom accountable party will be rebuilt later. Payback may rest on undisclosed headcount reduction — presenting this rollout without that stated risks a credibility break with technicians. Fine-tuning on unvalidated data would encode logged errors as ground truth. AI Act classification is unresolved and could change architecture requirements after the fact. One workstream is unresourced while the schedule slips; absorbing that gap into architecture (skipping trust-boundary or audit work) to hit a date is a decision, and it should be made visibly, not by default.

Next Steps: (1) Executive Sponsor names the Domain Owner within one week — nothing else proceeds credibly without this. (2) Value Realization Lead re-runs the business case against real pilot data, states the headcount assumption explicitly, within two weeks. (3) Field Ops Manager convenes resisting technicians and managers this week; findings feed the escalation design. (4) Data Readiness Lead validates a golden dataset sample against a stated accuracy threshold, two weeks. (5) Model Risk Lead audits pilot outputs for bias by equipment class and technician tenure, starting now. (6) Process Excellence Lead and Architect walk three disputed-diagnosis cases through a drafted escalation map. (7) Domain Owner and Compliance obtain a written AI Act determination before model selection is finalized. (8) Whoever owns the unresourced workstream escalates the gap to the Executive Sponsor this week, with a stated resourcing ask.
